text:
This looks like August 2011. Unemployment is 9.2%, the fed funds rate is about 0.08%, and the 10-year yield is 2.98% after a sharp fall. The VIX is 23.74, up 9 points in 3 months. Gold is up 7.5% in the month and 37% over 12 months. Headline CPI is 3.43%, which fits mid-2011, and core CPI is 1.64%.

The VIX points to a month a little earlier than August. In August 2011 the VIX ended near 25.2, and the 10-year yield ended near 2.2%, so the 10-year does not fit August. The 10-year at 2.98% fits June 2011 (about 3.16%) better, or possibly July (about 2.8%). Unemployment of 9.2% was reported for June and July, with the June figure at 9.1%, revised later. The 3m payroll average of 87k is consistent with June 2011, when payrolls were weak.

Several other readings do not fit June. US equities are down 4.7% over 3 months, but the S&P 500 was roughly flat in June 2011. Treasuries 7-10y are up 2.8% in the month, which is a big gain. The 10y yield is down 0.34 over 3 months, but from 3.3% in the spring to 2.98% is only a modest move. The VIX at 23.74 is also not a June reading, since it was about 16 in June.

July 2011 fits better: the 10y closed near 2.8%, gold gained about 7.5% in July (it reached 1,620 from 1,500), and US equities fell 2%. Equity three-month returns of -4.7% do not fit July exactly. The VIX ended July at about 25.

I settle on July 2011, with the figures roughly consistent but not exact.
